answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in a cryptographic attestation chain that spreads trust like a branching vine. Each node must forge identity proofs through a zero-knowledge prism, aggregating stake and verifications. Deploying duplicate identities triggers exponential capital exhaustion, imposing superlinear staking penalties O(2^k) on clustered swarms to make mass-spawning mathematically and economically ruinous.
